description: The state space already contains a 3-dimensional object, Sym^2(V), but it fails the Sym^2 gate because all SU(2) reps are self-dual; hence no summand of any V^(tensor n) can pass. Bean qou-8p1i.

computation.arithmetic: exact integer weight multisets; no floating point

data.verdict: a 3-dimensional object exists natively (Sym^2(V), the SU(2) adjoint) but fails the Sym^2 gate: Sym^2(3) = 5+1 has a singlet because the adjoint is self-dual, whereas SU(3)'s Sym^2(3) = 6 is irreducible
data.generalisation: every SU(2) representation is self-dual, so every summand of every tensor power of a 2-dimensional fibre is self-dual and none can pass the gate
data.scope: scope-(b) for 'some summand of V^(tensor n) with dim V = 2 passes the Sym^2 gate', excluded by self-duality of all SU(2) representations
data.consequence_for_T3b: 'inequivalent fibre objects' cannot mean different summands of V^(tensor n); it must mean genuinely non-isomorphic fibres, a Tannakian gerbe / multi-fibre-functor situation
not_claimed: that no 3-dimensional fibre exists anywhere in the framework -- only that it is not inside the tensor powers of the existing 2-dimensional one
anything about how to construct inequivalent fibres
